title: Vanishing in the universal curve test
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X & \xleftarrow{\;h\;} & Y\\
f\big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow e\\
S & \xleftarrow{\;g\;} & \operatorname{Spec}K
\end{array}
$$

be a base-change square where
$X\to S$ is an affine smooth morphism of relative dimension one (in
the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) and $X$ is affine, $S$ is
the spectrum of a
normal domain $A$ with
algebraically closed fraction
field $L$, and $K/L$ is an extension of algebraically closed fields.
The map $g$ is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by the given inclusions $A\subset L\subset K$. Let $d$ be an integer invertible on $S$. The coefficient $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ is the constant abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and higher direct images are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then

$$
R^qh_*(\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z)=0\qquad(q\geq1).
$$

proof.text: Put $n=|d|$. Since $A$ is a nonzero domain and $d$ is a unit, $n\geq1$; the ideals $(d)$ and $(n)$ in $\mathbf Z$ coincide and $n$ remains a unit after every restriction and field extension below. Thus we work with $M=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ without excluding negative integers $d$. By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $R^qh_*\underline M$ is associated with $P_q(U)=H^q(U\times_XY,\underline M)=H^q(U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K,\underline M)$. The equality of fibre products follows by composing the two Cartesian squares. It suffices to kill every such class after an etale cover; the elementary sheafification argument is given in the last step. Affine opens cover each etale object, so it suffices to start with affine $U$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: For affine etale $U\to X$, the composite $U\to S$ is smooth of relative dimension $0+1=1$ by [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence]; its fibre $C=U\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth of relative dimension one by the same node. It is affine: if $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, then $C=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AK)$. Smoothness gives local finite presentation; affineness makes $C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ quasi-compact and separated, hence finite type. To allow disconnected or empty $C$, use [lem-sc-smooth-curve-connected-coproduct] to decompose it into finitely many connected smooth curves $C_j$. Their inclusions are open and closed; being closed in affine $C$, each $C_j$ is affine. Apply [sbc-thm-cohomological-dimension-of-an-affine-curve] to each $C_j$ and only its $q>1$ clause. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-cohomology-assembly], $H^q(C,\underline M)=\prod_jH^q(C_j,\underline M)=0$ for $q>1$. The empty product is the zero abelian group.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: For $q=1$, apply [sbc-lem-slicing] to the smooth composite $U\to S$ from the preceding step. It gives a jointly surjective etale family $U_i\to U$, with $U_i\to V_i\to S$, both $U_i,V_i$ affine, $U_i\to V_i$ smooth with geometrically connected fibres and a section. Because $S$ and $V_i$ are affine, $V_i\to S$ is separated: its diagonal is induced by the surjection $\Gamma(V_i)\otimes_A\Gamma(V_i)\to\Gamma(V_i)$. Apply [sbc-lem-etale-over-normal] to the integral normal $S$, whose function field $L$ is separably closed. It writes $V_i$ as a disjoint union of open-and-closed summands $V_{i\alpha}$, each identified with an open of $S$. First restrict $U_i$ to $U_{i\alpha}=U_i\times_{V_i}V_{i\alpha}$; this is open and closed in the affine $U_i$, hence affine, and is still etale over $U$. Refine each nonempty $V_{i\alpha}$ by affine open subsets $W$; this avoids assuming an arbitrary open of $S$ affine. Put $C_W=U_{i\alpha}\times_{V_{i\alpha}}W$. This is affine, smooth with geometrically connected fibres and a section over $W$. Since $W\to S$ is an open immersion, $C_W=U_{i\alpha}\times_SW$; the relative dimension is one by the permanence node applied to the etale composite $U_{i\alpha}\to U\to X$ and base change to $W$. The $C_W\to U$ still form an etale covering. Each nonempty affine open $W$ is integral normal with function field $L$: its local rings are those of $S$, and its generic point has the same local ring $L$. The canonical geometric generic point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$ therefore factors through every such $W$. We may now work with one pair $(C,W)$ of this form and the restriction $\xi\in H^1(C_K,\underline M)$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: The generic fibre $C_L$ is a smooth separated curve over $L$, and it is connected and nonempty because $C\to W$ has geometrically connected fibres and a section. The map $C_K\to C_L$ is the base change for the given field extension $L\subseteq K$ (here the specified generic factorization of $g$ is essential). Apply [sbc-thm-algebraically-closed-invariance] in degree one; it supplies $\bar\xi\in H^1(C_L,\underline M)$ pulling back to $\xi$. By [sbc-prop-torsors-h1], $\bar\xi$ is represented by a finite etale $M$-torsor $P\to C_L$, naturally under pullback. Do not assume $P$ connected. For the next step fix the geometric base point $\sigma(\eta):\operatorname{Spec}L\to C_L$ and a point $p$ in the fibre of $P$ there; the fibre is nonempty by the torsor condition and is split by [lem-galois-geometric-fibre], since $L$ is algebraically closed.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: Here is the connected-component argument in the unit, rather than the incorrect claim that every torsor is connected. By [lem-fet-galois-category] and [thm-galois-abstract-equivalence], finite etale covers of connected $C_L$ are finite continuous $\pi_1(C_L,\sigma(\eta))$-sets. Identify the fibre of $P$ with $M$ using $p$. The monodromy is translation by the homomorphism $f_P$ of [sbc-prop-torsors-h1]. Put $G=\operatorname{im}f_P\subset M$. The subset $G\subset M$ is invariant and nonempty, so the equivalence realizes its inclusion as a finite etale subcover $Z\to P$. The orbit decomposition $M=\coprod_{a\in M/G}(a+G)$ shows $Z$ is an open-and-closed component. It is connected: a decomposition into two nonempty open-and-closed finite etale pieces would decompose the transitive $\pi_1$-set $G$ into two invariant subsets. Translations by $G$ commute with the monodromy and act simply transitively on its fibre; full faithfulness transports these automorphisms and their group laws to $Z$. Thus $Z\to C_L$ is a finite etale Galois cover with group $G$. The chosen label $0\in G$ is a point above $\sigma(\eta)$, rational over $L$ by [lem-galois-geometric-fibre]. Its degree $|G|$ divides $n=|M|$ by the partition into cosets, hence is a unit on $W$: if $n=|G|a$, an inverse is $a n^{-1}$. The map $Z\to P$ gives a section of $Z\times_{C_L}P\to Z$, namely $z\mapsto(z,z\mapsto P)$; the torsor is therefore trivial on $Z$, and the natural pointed bijection of [sbc-prop-torsors-h1] says $\bar\xi|_Z=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-spreading-finite-etale-galois] with base $W$ and curve $C$. All its hypotheses now hold: $W$ is affine, hence qcqs, integral normal; $C\to W$ is affine smooth, hence qcqs, has geometrically connected fibres and the restricted section; $|G|$ is invertible; and $Z$ has the required rational point over that section. Obtain a finite etale Galois cover $T\to C$ with $T_L\simeq Z$. It is surjective by its torsor condition, so it is an etale covering of $C$. Pulling $\bar\xi|_Z=0$ to $K$ gives $\xi|_{T_K}=0$. Explicitly, $T\times_CC_K\simeq T_L\times_LK\simeq Z\times_LK$; functoriality of cohomology identifies restriction of $\xi$ with pullback of $\bar\xi|_Z$. The torsor interpretation is natural by [sbc-prop-torsors-h1]. Composing these covers with $C\to U$ from slicing kills the original class on an etale cover of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, second proof: final universal curve-test argument

proof.text: For completeness the local killing criterion needs no extra vanishing theorem. If every element of an abelian presheaf $P$ is locally zero, any morphism $P\to F$ into a sheaf is zero: the image of each element restricts to zero on a cover, so is zero by the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom. Apply this to the sheafification unit $P\to P^\#$ of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The unit is zero, and its universal property says there is a unique map $P^\#\to P^\#$ factoring it. Both the identity and zero map do, so they agree, and $P^\#=0$. The preceding steps establish local killing of $P_q$ first on affine objects and hence on all objects by their affine open covers. Thus $R^qh_*\underline M=P_q^\#=0$ for every $q\geq1$.
